description: A technically proficient junior aiming for a career in high-performance computing and quantitative finance, prioritizing implementation efficiency and concurrency.

nodes.description: Review of operating system services, system calls, and the distinction between user and kernel mode.
nodes.personalizationRationale: Ensures that even students with strong_prior_exposure have a consistent baseline of formal OS terminology and structure.
nodes.title: OS Foundations & System Structure
Architectural Analysis: Microkernels vs. Monolithic Systems
nodes.personalizationRationale: Given the student's strong_prior_exposure, this node investigates architectural design decisions rather than just basic definitions.
nodes.description: A deep dive into the trade-offs between monolithic, microkernel, and hybrid kernel architectures in modern systems.

nodes.personalizationRationale: Required floor content for strong_prior_exposure students to master process management before moving to threading.
nodes.description: Exploration of the process abstraction, lifecycle, and fundamental IPC mechanisms like shared memory and message passing.
nodes.title: Processes & IPC Fundamentals

nodes.personalizationRationale: Builds on the student's strong_prior_exposure by examining the performance implications of IPC at scale.
nodes.description: Investigating performance overheads and synchronization challenges in high-frequency message-passing systems.
nodes.title: Advanced IPC & Performance Optimization
Threads & Threading Models
nodes.personalizationRationale: Core material for strong_prior_exposure students to understand the internal mapping of user threads to kernel threads.
nodes.description: Comparative analysis of multi-threading models and the implementation of threading libraries.
Evaluation of CPU scheduling algorithms including Round Robin, Priority Scheduling, and Multi-Level Feedback Queues.
nodes.personalizationRationale: Essential scheduling theory that students with strong_prior_exposure must master for the midterm exam.
nodes.title: CPU Scheduling Criteria & Algorithms
Midterm Review (Ch. 1-5)
nodes.description: Comprehensive review of chapters 1-5 covering OS structures, processes, and scheduling in preparation for the midterm.
nodes.personalizationRationale: Formal assessment checkpoint to ensure the student's strong_prior_exposure translates to exam readiness for the midterm.
Core synchronization primitives are mandatory for strong_prior_exposure students as they form the basis for project work.
nodes.description: Detailed study of the critical section problem and the use of mutex locks, semaphores, and monitors.
nodes.title: Process Synchronization & Primitives
Priority Inversion & Inheritance Protocols
nodes.description: Exploring the priority inversion problem and solutions like the priority inheritance protocol in real-time systems.
nodes.personalizationRationale: Challenges the strong_prior_exposure student with advanced synchronization edge cases used in real-world systems.

nodes.title: Deadlock Characterization & Prevention
nodes.description: Characterizing deadlock conditions and implementing prevention, avoidance (Banker's Algorithm), and detection strategies.
nodes.personalizationRationale: Required floor coverage of deadlock management for all students, including those with strong_prior_exposure.
Foundational memory concepts that must be reviewed by strong_prior_exposure students before virtual memory.
nodes.description: Introduction to physical memory management, including contiguous allocation, fragmentation, and the paging abstraction.
nodes.title: Physical Memory & Paging Structures
Virtual Memory & Page Replacement
nodes.personalizationRationale: Core virtual memory theory required for both the final exam and programming project delivery for strong_prior_exposure students.
nodes.description: Examination of demand paging, page replacement algorithms (LRU, Optimal), and the phenomenon of thrashing.

nodes.title: TLB Performance & Advanced Memory Hardware
nodes.description: Analysis of TLB performance, the impact of page sizes (HugePages), and hardware-level memory management optimizations.
nodes.personalizationRationale: Utilizes the student's strong_prior_exposure to explore the hardware-software interface of memory performance.

nodes.title: I/O Systems & Device Interfaces
nodes.description: Overview of I/O hardware, polling vs. interrupts, and the kernel I/O subsystem structure.
nodes.personalizationRationale: Standard curriculum floor for I/O systems to ensure strong_prior_exposure students understand kernel-level I/O.

nodes.title: File System Implementation & Reliability
nodes.personalizationRationale: Critical capstone topic for strong_prior_exposure students, focusing on the implementation details of persistent storage.
nodes.description: Design and implementation of file systems, including directory structures, allocation methods, and journaling for reliability.

nodes.title: Final Cumulative Review & Assessment
nodes.personalizationRationale: A mandatory cumulative assessment designed to verify mastery across all syllabus blocks for a student with strong_prior_exposure.
nodes.description: Cumulative review of all course material from OS structures to file systems in preparation for the final exam.
